topic: Hitler calling his Napoleon-tomb visit his happiest day, then invading Russia 129 years after Napoleon did
title: Hitler Called This His Happiest Day. Then He Repeated Napoleon's Exact Mistake
description: AI-narrated commentary on a real historical irony: Hitler called visiting Napoleon's tomb the greatest moment of his life, then invaded Russia almost exactly 129 years after Napoleon did, and it ended in the same kind of winter catastrophe. Sources in the description.

hook_candidates.text: Hitler's happiest day ever was standing at Napoleon's tomb, right before repeating his exact mistake.
What did Hitler do exactly 129 years after Napoleon first invaded Russia?
You'd think admiring Napoleon's tomb would stop a dictator from repeating Napoleon's mistake, but it didn't.
In June 1940, Hitler stood at Napoleon's tomb in Paris and called it the greatest moment of his life.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists dictators are strategic geniuses, because they want to show even Hitler couldn't escape repeating history.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume Hitler's happiest day at Napoleon's tomb would have stopped him from repeating Napoleon's exact mistake.
closing_comment: Napoleon and Hitler even repeated the same brutal winter collapse, 129 years apart.

sources.note: Confirms Hitler visited Napoleon's tomb in Paris in 1940, per Albert Speer's account.
Confirms Operation Barbarossa, Hitler's invasion of Russia, began June 22, 1941.
Confirms Napoleon's Grande Armee crossed into Russia on June 24, 1812.
